Full terminology expansions were not performed for broad/example/preferred bindings such as encounter-reason, service-type, v3-ActPriority, recurrence type, timezones, week-of-month, and days-of-week.
Narrative Appointment specification pages and recurrence guidance were not separately reviewed beyond generated StructureDefinition text.

scope.scopeNotesMd: This report analyzes local changes in the base `Appointment` resource StructureDefinition between the local R4 4.0.1 and R6 6.0.0-ballot4 core packages. It includes local element additions/removals/renames, datatype and reference-target changes, local invariants, terminology bindings directly attached to Appointment elements, and R6-to-R4 representability risks. It intentionally excludes inherited-only changes from `Element`, `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `BackboneElement`, and reusable datatypes except where a local Appointment element newly uses that datatype and the datatype shape is needed to explain the local change.
outOfScope: Inherited/base-artifact changes from Element, BackboneElement, Resource, DomainResource, and Extension, including base extension constraints and generated `mustSupport=false` decorations.
Resource-level `language` binding changes and DomainResource contained-resource/narrative text changes observed in the snapshot; these belong to Resource/DomainResource reports.
SearchParameter changes for Appointment, including R6 service-type-reference and recurrence-related search parameters; they are separate conformance artifacts.
Full datatype breaking-change analysis for CodeableReference, Annotation, VirtualServiceDetail, and other referenced datatypes/resources.
Implementation-guide profiles, operations, CapabilityStatements, and server behavior outside the base Appointment StructureDefinition.

narrativeReportMd:
# Appointment R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Appointment` keeps the same resource identity, but R6 contains multiple local wire-format breaks. The highest-impact changes are the replacement of several primitive or parallel fields with richer datatypes (`reason`, `participant.required`, `priority`, `patientInstruction`, `serviceType`, `note`) and the spelling correction from `cancelationReason` to `cancellationReason`.

## Scope
The analysis compared the local R4 and R6 `StructureDefinition-Appointment.json` files and supporting local terminology for Appointment statuses and participant required codes. Inherited Resource/DomainResource/Element changes were excluded from findings and listed out of scope.

## Main migration themes
R6 consistently moves Appointment toward richer typed structures: `CodeableReference` for concept-or-resource fields, `Annotation` for notes, boolean attendance requirements, broader request/actor references, and native recurrence/series metadata. These are mostly reasonable modeling improvements, but they break strict JSON validation and generated R4 models.

## Highest-impact findings
The most disruptive R4→R6 breaks are same-path or replacement datatype changes: `participant.required` code→boolean, `priority` unsignedInt→CodeableConcept, `patientInstruction` string→CodeableReference, `serviceType` CodeableConcept→CodeableReference, and `reasonCode`/`reasonReference`→`reason`. The new `app-5` invariant is also a hard validation tightening for records with `start > end`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important where no canonical mapping is computable from the supplied definitions: `information-only` participants, numeric priority to ActPriority, patient-instruction references, HealthcareService service types, unsupported reason targets, broader `basedOn`/actor targets, and recurrence-series downgrade.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several breaks could have been mitigated by transitional aliases, choice elements, or deprecated old fields. The tradeoff would have been a more complex base resource with duplicate representations. Optional R6 additions are not R4→R6 breaking, but they create substantial R6→R4 round-trip gaps.

## Follow-up analysis
Datatype reports for `CodeableReference`, `Annotation`, and `VirtualServiceDetail`, terminology expansion review, and Appointment SearchParameter analysis would improve migration planning confidence.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Appointment` has hard local breaking changes despite stable resource identity. The main concerns are renamed/removed fields, primitive-to-complex datatype replacements, loss of the `information-only` participant code, and R6-only recurrence/request/actor expressiveness. The top uncertainty is exact terminology and business-rule mapping for priority, reason, service type, and recurrence workflows.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a structural transform, not a version-label update. Most old data can be upgraded only by renaming or wrapping values (`cancelationReason`, `comment`, `reasonCode`, `serviceType`, `patientInstruction`) and by applying domain policy for semantic changes (`participant.required`, `priority`, unsupported reason targets). Downgrade from R6 needs extensions or manual review for recurrence, new reference targets, and new operational fields.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for StructureDefinition-level changes because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and compared directly, and relevant local CodeSystems for status/participant codes were checked. Confidence is lower for migration justification and terminology semantics because no official diff, Jira rationale, narrative guidance, or full terminology expansions were supplied.

findings.title: `cancelationReason` was renamed to `cancellationReason`

oldState.summary: R4 serialized the cancellation reason under the misspelled `cancelationReason` element.

semanticText.definition: The coded reason for the appointment being cancelled.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 exposes a local element named `Appointment.cancelationReason` with one `l` after `cance`. Its cardinality, type, summary flag, and example binding otherwise match the later element.

newState.summary: R6 serializes the same concept as `cancellationReason`.

semanticText.definition: The coded reason for the appointment being cancelled.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 corrects the spelling to `Appointment.cancellationReason`. This is a local resource element rename, not an inherited base change.

facts.note: The payload shape is preserved after renaming.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The short text, definition, cardinality, type, binding, and summary flag match closely; the only material local identity change is spelling.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct wire-format and generated-code break. An R4 JSON instance containing `cancelationReason` uses a property that is unknown in the R6 base resource. R6 instances using `cancellationReason` likewise need a spelling transform before R4 validation or parsing.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Cancellation/no-show workflows can affect reporting, billing, and operational follow-up; dropping the reason during migration can change downstream business behavior.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Correcting the spelling is understandable, but the breakage is disproportionate for a spelling-only element rename. Retaining the nonoptimal R4 name while fixing the definition text and invariant would preserve existing instances and still keep the same clinical meaning.
justification.inferredGoal: Correct the element spelling and align the invariant expression with `cancellationReason`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 `cancelationReason` element in base R6 with corrected definitions and invariants, documenting the misspelling as historical.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would leave `Appointment.cancelationReason` as the canonical element in R6 and update narrative, comments, and invariants around it. A second correctly spelled alias could also be added, but that would create duplicate same-resource representations for the same fact; simply living with the old spelling is the cleaner compatibility path.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves a misspelled core element name, but avoids a hard wire-format break and avoids duplicate reason fields.

evidence.detail: R4 contains local element `Appointment.cancelationReason`.
R6 contains local element `Appointment.cancellationReason`.
The R6 invariant refers to `cancellationReason` and status `noshow`/`cancelled`.

examples.examplesMd: The example focuses on the renamed property. A migration can usually be lossless by moving the `CodeableConcept` value to `cancellationReason`.

findings.narrativeMd: The cancellation reason element was renamed from the R4 misspelling `cancelationReason` to `cancellationReason`. Although the value type and binding are stable, the JSON property and generated model member change. Strict R6 parsers will not accept the R4 property unless they implement a cross-version transform.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance that is otherwise valid and contains `cancelationReason` is not valid against the R6 base `Appointment` shape because that element no longer exists. Conversely, an R6 `cancellationReason` must be renamed to round-trip to R4. This is a schema/codegen break rather than a terminology break.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `cancelationReason` to `cancellationReason` before R6 validation. The transform is normally lossless for the element value. Test both `cancelled` and `noshow` statuses because R6's local `app-4` invariant uses the corrected property and the canonical `noshow` code.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The correction is understandable, but it could have been less disruptive if the R6 resource accepted the old spelling as a deprecated alias during transition. FHIR base resources generally do not support synonym element names, so downstream cross-version tooling has to carry the compatibility layer.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: R4's local `app-4` text/expression used `no-show` in one place even though the AppointmentStatus code system uses `noshow`; this report treats that as part of the spelling/correction cluster, not as a separate local breaking finding.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is a same-concept spelling rename from the R4 wire element `cancelationReason` to R6 `cancellationReason`. Existing R4 instances and generated client/server models using the R4 name will not be accepted by an R6 base parser without a transform, while the clinical meaning and type remain essentially the same. Because the change is a spelling correction rather than a new capability, the compatibility cost is disproportionate to the base-model benefit.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition has `Appointment.cancelationReason` 0..1 CodeableConcept.
R6 StructureDefinition has `Appointment.cancellationReason` 0..1 CodeableConcept and no R4-spelled element.
The existing report classifies this as High impact and says a backward-compatible alternative is available.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 status is FMM 3 / trial-use, so Appointment has meaningful deployed-stability expectations even though it is not normative. That raises the bar for a spelling-only wire break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 JSON/XML using `cancelationReason` is not the R6 element name, and generated code property names change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design exists: retain the historical misspelled element name and correct the definition, or keep it as a deprecated alias if the FHIR format allowed that pattern. The tradeoff is carrying an awkward spelling, but that is modest compared with a hard rename on a mature scheduling resource.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: I agree with the existing High impact and the existing Yes/avoidable alternative judgment.

findings.title: `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` were replaced by `reason` CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 split appointment reasons into separate coded and reference arrays.

binding.description: The Reason for the appointment to take place.

semanticText.definition: Coded or referenced reason the appointment is scheduled.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 has `reasonCode` for `CodeableConcept` values and `reasonReference` for resource references. They are independent arrays with different JSON property names.

newState.summary: R6 uses one repeating `reason` element of type `CodeableReference`.

binding.description: The Reason for the appointment to take place.

semanticText.definition: The reason that this appointment is being scheduled; can be coded or specified using another resource.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 collapses the two R4 elements into `Appointment.reason`, whose datatype has `concept` and `reference` children. Existing R4 JSON cannot be accepted without reshaping.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 element has the same broad definition and encounter-reason binding as R4 `reasonCode`, while its `CodeableReference.reference` side replaces `reasonReference`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Both old element names disappear and the datatype wrapper changes. R4 payloads with `reasonCode` or `reasonReference` fail R6 structural validation, and R6 `reason` entries are not cleanly represented in R4 without splitting each entry into either `reasonCode` or `reasonReference`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reason data can drive admission diagnosis, scheduling triage, reporting, and downstream clinical context. Loss or misclassification can have clinical and billing consequences.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Unifying coded and referenced reasons as CodeableReference is a coherent R6 modeling goal. A less-breaking transition was possible, but keeping the old parallel elements beside the new one would preserve exactly the duplication and disagreement risk the new model is trying to remove.
justification.inferredGoal: Unify coded and referenced reasons with `CodeableReference`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `reason` CodeableReference while retaining deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` for a transition period.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The partial alternative is to keep `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` valid in base R6 and add `reason` for new content. That covers existing R4 instances, but implementers and validators would need rules for cases where old and new reason fields both appear, and the deprecated representations might persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve old payloads but create duplicate reason representations and conflict-resolution rules.

evidence.detail: R4 has `reasonCode` as `CodeableConcept` with preferred `encounter-reason` binding.
R4 has `reasonReference` as a repeating Reference element.
R6 has one repeating `reason` element of type `CodeableReference`.
R6 `CodeableReference` serializes the concept and reference alternatives as child elements, not as a bare CodeableConcept or Reference.

examples.examplesMd: A typical transform wraps each R4 `reasonCode` as `reason.concept` and each supported R4 `reasonReference` as `reason.reference`. Target-profile differences are covered in a separate finding.

findings.narrativeMd: Appointment reasons moved from two separate R4 arrays to one R6 `CodeableReference` array. This is not just a rename: the JSON object shape changes because coded content must sit under `reason[].concept` and referenced content under `reason[].reference`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances containing either old property are old-valid/new-invalid unless transformed. R6 instances can contain mixed concept/reference entries in one ordered array; converting back to R4 requires splitting entries, and ordering or one-to-one pairing semantics may not survive if an implementation attached meaning to the original order.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `reasonCode[*]` to `reason[*].concept` and supported `reasonReference[*]` to `reason[*].reference`. Validate target resource types after mapping. Downgrade tools should split R6 `reason` entries back into the two R4 arrays and record any unsupported target references in extensions or manual-review queues.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A less-breaking design could have added `reason` while retaining deprecated `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` aliases. That would have protected old wire payloads but created redundant paths for the same concept and possible disagreement between old and new fields.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 separates reasons into `reasonCode` and `reasonReference`; R6 consolidates them into repeatable `reason` CodeableReference. This is a real wire and generated-model break, but it is a common R6 modeling pattern that removes parallel reason fields and gives each reason one code-or-reference representation. The path-level migration for ordinary R4 coded reasons and references is mostly mechanical, with target-profile changes handled separately in the dedicated finding.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition has `Appointment.reasonCode` CodeableConcept and `Appointment.reasonReference` Reference.
R6 StructureDefinition has `Appointment.reason` 0..* CodeableReference.
The existing report classifies this as High impact with a Partial alternative.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 / trial-use makes the break important to call out, especially because appointment reasons are operationally meaningful, but the content is not normative and the R6 consolidation has a coherent migration story.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: old `reasonCode`/`reasonReference` properties are not the R6 wire shape; reverse conversion can lose CodeableReference grouping if R6 instances use paired concept/reference semantics.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` while adding `reason`, but that creates duplicate reason representations and conflict-resolution rules. That tradeoff is significant enough that the breaking consolidation is probably acceptable.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: I agree with the existing High impact and Partial less-breaking-alternative judgment, while treating the target-profile removal as the separate reasonReference finding.

findings.title: Reason reference targets changed: ImmunizationRecommendation removed, DiagnosticReport added

oldState.summary: R4 reason references allowed Condition, Procedure, Observation, and ImmunizationRecommendation.
oldState.narrativeMd: After accounting for the structural merge, R4 allowed `ImmunizationRecommendation` as an appointment reason reference.

newState.summary: R6 `reason` references allow Condition, DiagnosticReport, Procedure, and Observation.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds `DiagnosticReport` but does not list `ImmunizationRecommendation` as a target for `Appointment.reason`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: This compares the reference side of R4 `reasonReference` to the reference side of R6 `reason` after the CodeableReference migration.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The structural reason merge already breaks raw R4 instances. In addition, a migrated R4 `ImmunizationRecommendation` reason reference has no allowed R6 target, while an R6 `DiagnosticReport` reason reference has no R4 target. Strict validators and generated reference-target checks can reject these cases.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reason references can affect clinical interpretation of why the appointment exists; unsupported target substitutions may lose specificity.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding DiagnosticReport appears reasonable, but the supplied computable evidence does not explain why ImmunizationRecommendation had to be removed. Because reference target widening could have preserved the R4 target and still added the new R6 target, the breaking portion is not clearly justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Refine the set of resources considered appropriate appointment reasons.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add DiagnosticReport as an R6 reason target while retaining ImmunizationRecommendation from R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design is a widened R6 target set: Condition, Procedure, Observation, ImmunizationRecommendation, and DiagnosticReport. The tradeoff is a looser semantic boundary for appointment reasons, but that is a moderate conformance cost compared with rejecting valid R4 ImmunizationRecommendation reason references.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps a broader target list, but avoids invalidating R4 reason references without duplicate fields.

evidence.detail: R4 target profiles include `ImmunizationRecommendation`.
R6 target profiles include `DiagnosticReport` but not `ImmunizationRecommendation`.

examples.examplesMd: The old-valid example is also affected by the structural reason merge; this finding isolates the target-profile issue that remains after a field-shape transform.

findings.narrativeMd: The allowed resource targets for appointment reasons changed. `ImmunizationRecommendation` is no longer an allowed reason target in R6, while `DiagnosticReport` is newly allowed. This matters for validators and for downgrade/upgrade transforms that otherwise know how to wrap references in `CodeableReference`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 `reasonReference` to `ImmunizationRecommendation` cannot be made R6-valid by simply moving it to `reason.reference`; the target profile is outside the R6 set. An R6 `DiagnosticReport` reason has the inverse R6-to-R4 problem. Both directions may require extensions or domain-specific substitution.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory existing `reasonReference` targets before migration. Map Condition, Procedure, and Observation mechanically. Queue ImmunizationRecommendation for manual review or extension-based retention. For R6-to-R4, handle DiagnosticReport references explicitly, such as by moving them to `supportingInformation` with a reason-link extension if the business meaning must be preserved.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The least-disruptive alternative would have preserved the R4 target set and added DiagnosticReport. Without narrative rationale, it is unclear whether removing ImmunizationRecommendation was intentional tightening or an oversight.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The problematic part of this finding is not the addition of DiagnosticReport as a reason target; it is that R4 Appointment reasons could reference ImmunizationRecommendation and R6 no longer permits that target through the new `reason` CodeableReference. R4 instances scheduling or explaining an appointment from an immunization recommendation become invalid even after the structural CodeableReference migration unless they are remapped to a different target or extension. Retaining the old target while adding new ones appears low cost.
keyEvidence: R4 `Appointment.reasonReference` includes ImmunizationRecommendation among allowed targets.
R6 `Appointment.reason` CodeableReference includes DiagnosticReport but omits ImmunizationRecommendation.
R4 maturity map shows ImmunizationRecommendation is FMM 1 / trial-use; the removed target is low maturity, but it is still a public-health/immunization use case.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Appointment itself is FMM 3 / trial-use, so changing an allowed reason target on this resource deserves scrutiny. The removed target resource is only FMM 1, which softens likely deployment breadth but does not eliminate concern because retaining a reference target is cheap and immunization scheduling can be safety/public-health relevant.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Appointment whose reasonReference points to ImmunizationRecommendation has no base-valid R6 reason target for that same reference.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design is straightforward: keep ImmunizationRecommendation as an allowed R6 reason target and add DiagnosticReport. The tradeoff is a broader target list, but that is much less disruptive than invalidating an existing target without a clear replacement.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: I agree with the existing High impact and Yes/not-clearly-justified alternative judgment.

findings.title: `comment` string was replaced by repeating `note` Annotation

oldState.summary: R4 had one optional string comment.
oldState.narrativeMd: `Appointment.comment` was a scalar string intended for internal scheduling comments and guidance when dates were not yet set.

newState.narrativeMd: `Appointment.note` can repeat and can carry Annotation metadata such as author/time in addition to text. The R6 `description` and `patientInstruction` definitions now point to `note` instead of `comment`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The short text and comments line up directly: both represent additional appointment comments, but R6 uses the standard `Annotation` datatype and permits repeats.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The old JSON property is removed and the value changes from a primitive string to an object/array of Annotation objects. Strict parsers and generated clients must rename and reshape the data.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Operational comments often contain instructions for staff or scheduling context; dropping them can affect appointment handling.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving from a single string to Annotation supports multiple notes and note metadata, which is a reasonable model improvement. A transition design could preserve old instances, but it would carry two comment mechanisms with overlapping semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add repeating `note` Annotation while retaining deprecated `comment` string.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The partial alternative is to keep `comment` valid and introduce `note` for richer content. That preserves simple R4 comments, but base R6 would need reconciliation rules when both appear, and deprecated free-text comments might continue to accumulate rather than moving to Annotation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids immediate breaks but leaves overlapping comment fields with ordering, metadata, and conflict ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 `comment` is `string` 0..1.
R6 `note` is `Annotation` 0..*.
R6 guidance says detailed information should be put in the `note` field.
evidence.quote: Detailed or expanded information should be put in the note field.

oldValidNewInvalidJson.comment: Patient should proceed directly to infusion room.

note.text: Patient should proceed directly to infusion room.

examples.examplesMd: The R4-to-R6 transform can usually wrap the old string as `note[0].text`, but R6 note metadata and multiple notes are not losslessly representable in R4's single string.

findings.narrativeMd: Appointment comments changed from one primitive string to repeating `Annotation` notes. This is a material serialization and generated-model change even though the human-facing meaning is similar.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `comment` is new-invalid because R6 no longer defines that element. An R6 instance with multiple notes, author, or timestamp cannot be faithfully downgraded to the single R4 string without concatenation or data loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `comment` to `note[0].text` for straightforward upgrades. Downgrade tooling should define a deterministic policy for multiple notes and Annotation metadata, such as preserving the full R6 notes in an extension and populating R4 `comment` with a human-readable summary.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A compatibility-preserving design could have introduced `note` and kept `comment` deprecated. That would reduce breakage but keep two comment mechanisms with overlapping semantics. The R6 design favors a cleaner standard note datatype.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `comment` was a single string; R6 uses repeatable `note` Annotation. That breaks old wire instances and code, and comments can contain operationally important scheduling information. Still, the R6 model gives comments a standard Annotation shape with author/time metadata and repeats, which is a real functional improvement rather than a rename-only change.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition has `Appointment.comment` 0..1 string.
R6 StructureDefinition has `Appointment.note` 0..* Annotation.
The existing report classifies this as High impact with a Partial alternative.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 / trial-use means existing appointment comments should not be dismissed, but trial-use status leaves room for a targeted representation improvement when the old value can be migrated into `note.text`.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: old `comment` is not an R6 element; reverse conversion from multiple or attributed annotations to one string is potentially lossy.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept deprecated `comment` beside `note`, but that would create overlapping comment channels, ordering ambiguity, and conflict rules. The better Annotation model makes the break probably acceptable.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: I agree with the existing High impact and Partial less-breaking-alternative judgment.

findings.title: `participant.required` changed from required code enum to boolean

oldState.summary: R4 used a code bound to required | optional | information-only.

binding.description: Is the Participant required to attend the appointment.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 required binding disappears because the element is no longer coded in R6. The former `information-only` code has no boolean value.

semanticText.definition: Whether this participant is required to be present at the meeting.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented attendance requirement as a string code. The required value set included an `information-only` state for people/resources the appointment is about but who are not expected to attend.

newState.summary: R6 uses an optional boolean; false means optional, and information-only is modeled using `subject` instead.

semanticText.short: The participant is required to attend (optional when false)
semanticText.definition: Whether this participant is required to be present at the meeting. If false, the participant is optional.
semanticText.comment: For the use-case ... formerly done prior to R5 with required='information-only'.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the path but changes the JSON primitive from code/string to boolean. The R6 comment instructs implementers to use `Appointment.subject` and omit a participant for the former `information-only` case.

facts.note: No boolean equivalent; R6 guidance points to `Appointment.subject`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a same-path primitive type change. Existing JSON strings such as `required`, `optional`, and `information-only` are invalid where R6 expects a boolean. The former `information-only` value also requires a structural/semantic migration rather than a simple boolean mapping.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Participant requirement affects scheduling workflows, invitations, and whether a patient/group should appear as an attendee versus the subject of discussion.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of separating actual attendance from subject-of-discussion is reasonable, especially for the former `information-only` code. A compatibility path exists, but it would continue to allow the old mixed semantic model that R6 is explicitly trying to clean up.
justification.inferredGoal: Clarify attendance semantics and move non-attending subject context to `Appointment.subject`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 code element or add a new boolean while keeping the code for transition, with `information-only` deprecated and redirected to `subject` guidance.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could keep the required/optional/information-only code and add guidance or a separate boolean. This is only a partial alternative because it either keeps `information-only` participants valid or creates parallel boolean/code states, both of which can confuse validation and scheduling behavior.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old data but keeps tri-state attendance semantics and subject-vs-attendee ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 type is `code` with required participantrequired value set.
R4 participantrequired CodeSystem contains `required`, `optional`, and `information-only`.
evidence.quote: information-only: participant is excluded from the appointment

evidence.detail: R6 type is `boolean` and no terminology binding is present.
R6 says former `information-only` use should be modeled with `subject` and not as a participant.
evidence.quote: formerly done prior to R5 with required='information-only'

examples.examplesMd: `required` can often map to `true` and `optional` to `false`; `information-only` requires business logic because the subject may not be an attendee in R6.

findings.narrativeMd: The same path changed from a required-bound code to a boolean. This breaks parsers immediately and removes the explicit `information-only` enum, shifting that use case to the newer `subject` element.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 strings are invalid R6 booleans. R6 booleans can be downgraded only approximately (`true`→`required`, `false`→`optional`), while the old `information-only` state must be inferred from `subject` and participant absence if a downgrade is attempted.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `required` to `true` and `optional` to `false`. Treat `information-only` as a manual-review or domain-rule case: move the referenced patient/group to `Appointment.subject` when appropriate and avoid creating an attending participant solely to preserve the old enum value. Add tests for all three R4 codes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been less disruptive by retaining the code binding or adding a new boolean beside it. However, the R6 comment indicates an intentional semantic cleanup, and preserving `information-only` would keep mixing attendance with subject-of-discussion.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Changing `participant.required` from a three-code element to a boolean loses the explicit R4 `information-only` state at the same path. R6 guidance can move some information-only subjects out of participant handling, but that is not a pure type migration and can be expert- or workflow-dependent, especially when old data used participant entries to carry non-attending but relevant actors. The boolean simplification may be sensible, but the base break looks stronger than necessary for FMM 3 Appointment data.
keyEvidence: R4 `Appointment.participant.required` is a code bound to required/optional/information-only semantics.
R6 `Appointment.participant.required` is boolean.
The existing report classifies this as High impact and identifies only a Partial compatible alternative.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 / trial-use gives participant-attendance semantics a moderate stability expectation because they are central to scheduling. The resource is not normative, but a same-path tri-state-to-boolean collapse needs a stronger migration story.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid, runtime/API/codegen, and semantic loss: R4 code values are not booleans, and `information-only` is not represented by the new boolean alone.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could retain the R4 code for a transition period, add a new boolean, or keep `information-only` as a deprecated computable value while steering new instances toward `subject`. The tradeoff is carrying older attendance semantics, but that seems preferable to forcing a lossy boolean migration without an exact base mapping.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the existing High impact, but I rate the alternative as more compelling than the existing Probably justified/Partial assessment because of the `information-only` loss.

findings.title: `priority` changed from unsigned integer to CodeableConcept

oldState.summary: R4 `priority` was an optional `unsignedInt` using iCalendar-style 0/1..9 semantics in the definition.

semanticText.definition: The priority of the appointment ... iCal Standard specifies 0 as undefined, 1 as highest, 9 as lowest priority.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represents priority as a numeric primitive. The definition references iCalendar ordering but there is no terminology binding.

newState.summary: R6 `priority` is a `CodeableConcept` with example v3 ActPriority binding.

binding.description: Indicates the urgency of the appointment.

semanticText.definition: The priority of the appointment ... iCal Standard specifies 0 as undefined, 1 as highest, 9 as lowest priority.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses a coded concept object while retaining text that still references the older numeric iCalendar priority scale.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A numeric R4 value is invalid where R6 expects a CodeableConcept object. There is no computable ConceptMap in the supplied inputs that maps iCalendar numeric priorities to v3 ActPriority codes, so both upgrade and downgrade can be lossy.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Priority may affect scheduling triage and rescheduling decisions. Incorrect mapping can change operational urgency.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving toward coded priority concepts is reasonable, but the available evidence does not provide a canonical mapping from the R4 iCalendar-style number to the R6 CodeableConcept. Because an additive coded element could have supported richer priorities while preserving numeric instances, the hard type replacement is not clearly justified.
justification.inferredGoal: Move from a narrow numeric scale to coded urgency concepts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the unsigned integer priority and add an optional coded priority element or choice-like extension point.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The partial alternative is to leave `priority` as unsignedInt and add a distinct coded priority element for R6 adopters. This would preserve R4 payloads, but systems would need precedence and consistency rules when both numeric and coded priorities are present, and cross-system analytics would still need mapping guidance.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves numeric compatibility but creates parallel urgency representations without a universal numeric-to-code map.

evidence.detail: R4 type is `unsignedInt` with no binding.
R6 type is `CodeableConcept` with example v3 ActPriority binding.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example uses an ActPriority code illustratively; the report did not find a local ConceptMap from R4 numeric priority to v3 codes.

findings.narrativeMd: `Appointment.priority` changed JSON shape from a number to a coded concept. Numeric values that formerly carried iCalendar priority cannot be parsed by R6 as-is, and coded R6 priority cannot be downgraded to an R4 integer without a policy mapping.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is an old-valid/new-invalid type break for any R4 instance with a numeric priority. It is also a high R6-to-R4 representability risk because a CodeableConcept can contain multiple codings/text that do not correspond to a single unsigned integer.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define an explicit local mapping from numeric priority values to codes and back before migration. Preserve the original numeric value in an extension if the mapping is not reversible. Test boundary values 0, 1, and 9 and any local values outside the iCalendar range.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A choice type such as priority[x] or an additive coded element would have supported both numeric and coded representations. The tradeoff is a more complicated API and the need to resolve conflicts between parallel representations.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 numeric priority becomes an R6 CodeableConcept priority. That is a hard same-path type change with no universally safe numeric-to-code mapping, and urgency/priority can affect scheduling operations. Moving to coded priority may be desirable, but a base-compatible transition path seems important here.
keyEvidence: R4 `Appointment.priority` is unsignedInt.
R6 `Appointment.priority` is CodeableConcept with an example ActPriority binding.
The existing report classifies this as High impact and says the change is not clearly justified with a Partial alternative.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 / trial-use raises compatibility expectations for operational priority. The trial-use status and R4 feedback-oriented text temper the concern somewhat, but do not solve the lack of a computable mapping.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: an R4 integer value is not an R6 CodeableConcept; reverse conversion from arbitrary coded priorities to a single unsigned integer is policy-dependent.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could keep numeric priority and add a coded priority element, or define a transition choice with explicit mapping guidance. That creates parallel urgency representations, but the current direct replacement has enough migration ambiguity to deserve reconsideration.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: I agree with the existing High impact and with the existing concern that a less-breaking design is at least partially available.

findings.title: `patientInstruction` changed from single string to repeating CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 had a single optional patient-facing instruction string.

semanticText.definition: Appointment.patientInstructions is used to capture patient facing information about the Appointment.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 stores patient-facing appointment instructions as one primitive string.

newState.summary: R6 uses repeating CodeableReference values that can point to DocumentReference, Binary, or Communication.

semanticText.definition: Appointment.patientInstructions is used to capture patient facing information about the Appointment.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 supports multiple instructions and either coded/text concepts or references to instruction-bearing resources.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A primitive string is not valid as an R6 CodeableReference array entry. R6 references to external instruction resources have no R4 core element equivalent, so downgrade is lossy without extensions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Patient instructions can directly affect preparation, safety, consent, and appointment success; losing or flattening them is clinically and operationally important.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Richer and externally referenced patient instructions are a plausible R6 goal, and a single CodeableReference-based model is clearer for new implementations. The less-breaking alternative would preserve old strings, but it would introduce overlapping ways to carry patient-facing instructions.
justification.inferredGoal: Support richer and externally referenced patient instructions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 string and add a richer repeating CodeableReference or reference field for structured instructions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The partial alternative is to keep the string field valid and add a new rich instruction element. It protects R4 free text, but R6 validators and applications would need to handle conflicts, ordering, and possible duplication between string instructions and referenced or coded instructions.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves simple text but leaves duplicate patient-instruction channels and safety-sensitive reconciliation issues.

evidence.detail: R4 type is `string` 0..1.
R6 type is `CodeableReference` 0..* targeting DocumentReference, Binary, and Communication.
CodeableReference stores text/codes under `concept` and resource links under `reference`.

examples.examplesMd: Wrapping old text into `CodeableReference.concept.text` is a plausible upgrade rule, but R6 reference entries cannot be represented in R4's single string without summarization or extensions.

findings.narrativeMd: Patient instructions became a repeating CodeableReference. This changes the wire representation and greatly expands expressiveness, but existing R4 strings must be reshaped before R6 validation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 string values are invalid under the R6 element type. R6 can represent references to DocumentReference, Binary, or Communication; R4 has no matching core field and can only retain a flattened text summary or an extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For simple text, map to `patientInstruction[0].concept.text`. Preserve referenced instruction resources with extensions or related resources when downgrading. Review patient-safety workflows to ensure preparation instructions are not dropped during conversion.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: An additive richer element or choice type would have allowed existing string payloads to survive. R6 instead reuses CodeableReference, favoring a single richer model over compatibility with the primitive representation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `patientInstruction` was a single string; R6 makes patient instructions repeatable CodeableReference values that can carry coded instructions or reference instruction-bearing resources. This is a hard type and cardinality change on safety-relevant patient-facing text, but simple R4 strings can be preserved as CodeableConcept text and the R6 model supports richer, reusable instructions that R4 could not represent well.
keyEvidence: R4 `Appointment.patientInstruction` is 0..1 string.
R6 `Appointment.patientInstruction` is 0..* CodeableReference targeting DocumentReference, Binary, or Communication.
The existing report classifies this as High impact with a Partial compatible alternative.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 / trial-use means patient-instruction compatibility matters, especially because the content can affect patient behavior. The resource is still trial-use, and the R6 representation has a strong safety/expressiveness rationale when migrated carefully.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid, runtime/API/codegen, and R6-to-R4 loss: old strings must be wrapped; R6 referenced or multiple instructions cannot always be downgraded to a single R4 string without loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained the string and added a richer instruction field, but that would create duplicate patient-instruction channels with safety-sensitive reconciliation problems. The richer unified representation is probably worth the migration burden.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: I agree with the existing High impact and Partial less-breaking-alternative judgment.

findings.title: `serviceType` changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(HealthcareService)

oldState.summary: R4 used repeating CodeableConcept values with an example service-type binding.

semanticText.definition: The specific service that is to be performed during this appointment.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `serviceType` is a direct CodeableConcept array.

newState.summary: R6 uses repeating CodeableReference values targeting HealthcareService, retaining the service-type example binding for concepts.

semanticText.definition: The specific service that is to be performed during this appointment.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `serviceType` can carry either a concept or a reference to a specific HealthcareService. The concept must be nested under `concept`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 CodeableConcept array entries are not valid R6 CodeableReference entries unless wrapped as `concept`. R6 references to HealthcareService have no direct R4 `serviceType` representation.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Service type is often used for scheduling, routing, search, and analytics. Losing the distinction between a type code and a concrete service can affect workflows.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing an appointment to reference a HealthcareService is a reasonable improvement, but replacing the existing CodeableConcept wire shape was not the only way to achieve it. A separate optional reference would preserve common R4 serviceType data while still supporting the core new R6 capability.
justification.inferredGoal: Allow service type to be either coded or linked to HealthcareService.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `serviceType` as CodeableConcept and add an optional HealthcareService reference element for the new linkage use case.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would leave `Appointment.serviceType` unchanged for coded service types and add a new optional reference such as a HealthcareService link. The tradeoff is that code and reference values can diverge, but that coordination burden is moderate and familiar compared with forcing every R4 coded value through a new CodeableReference wrapper.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds a coordination rule between a service type code and a concrete service reference, but avoids breaking existing coded serviceType instances.

evidence.detail: R4 type is `CodeableConcept` 0..*.
R6 type is `CodeableReference` 0..* targeting HealthcareService.

examples.examplesMd: Coded R4 service types can be wrapped under `concept`; R6 references to HealthcareService require a downgrade policy.

findings.narrativeMd: `serviceType` kept its name and cardinality but changed datatype to CodeableReference. This is easy to miss because the element path is stable; generated classes and raw JSON still change substantially.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 `serviceType` CodeableConcept object such as `{"text":"Follow-up"}` is invalid as an R6 CodeableReference because the concept must be nested. R6 reference-valued service types cannot be represented in R4 without losing the link or using an extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap existing `serviceType[*]` values as `serviceType[*].concept`. For R6-to-R4, either derive a CodeableConcept from the referenced HealthcareService or preserve the reference in an extension; verify search/index behavior because R6 also has reference-aware service-type search parameters outside this resource report.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The same goal could have been achieved with a separate optional reference element, preserving the CodeableConcept shape. CodeableReference is cleaner but forces all existing coded instances through a structural transform.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `serviceType` was a CodeableConcept; R6 changes it to CodeableReference so it can point to HealthcareService. This breaks existing coded service-type data even though coded service category/type is a common scheduling and search axis. Unlike some CodeableReference migrations, the less-breaking design of retaining the coded service type while adding a concrete HealthcareService link is straightforward.
keyEvidence: R4 `Appointment.serviceType` is CodeableConcept.
R6 `Appointment.serviceType` is CodeableReference with HealthcareService as the reference target.
The existing report classifies this as High impact and says a backward-compatible alternative is available.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 / trial-use increases the stability expectation for service classification in appointment scheduling. Trial-use status leaves room for model improvements, but not without a strong reason to replace a widely usable coded element.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid, runtime/API/codegen, and R6-to-R4 loss: old coded values must be wrapped into CodeableReference, and R6 HealthcareService references may not downgrade cleanly to a CodeableConcept.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could keep `serviceType` as CodeableConcept and add a separate HealthcareService reference element. The tradeoff is keeping a coordination rule between code and service reference, but that is lower cost than invalidating existing coded serviceType instances.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: I agree with the existing High impact and Yes/probably-avoidable alternative judgment.

findings.title: New error invariant requires `start` to be less than or equal to `end`

oldState.summary: R4 required start/end presence consistency but did not include a local ordering invariant.

constraints.human: Either start and end are specified, or neither
Only proposed or cancelled appointments can be missing start/end dates

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 checked that `start` and `end` appeared together, and that most statuses had both, but did not reject reversed instants at the Appointment StructureDefinition level.

newState.summary: R6 adds local error invariant `app-5`: `start.exists() implies start <= end`.

constraints.human: The start must be less than or equal to the end

newState.narrativeMd: R6 introduces an error-level validation rule that rejects appointments whose end is before the start.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation tightening. An R4 instance with both instants present but `start` after `end` can satisfy R4's local constraints and fail R6's new error invariant. Runtime model shapes do not change.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reversed start/end times can cause scheduling, billing-duration, and availability errors; the new rule likely catches bad data rather than intended content.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is basic temporal consistency, and an appointment whose start is after its end is usually erroneous scheduling data. A warning would be less breaking but would not satisfy the base-model goal of making reversed intervals invalid, so the error-level invariant is justified despite rejecting some bad historical R4 data.
justification.inferredGoal: Prevent appointments with negative duration or reversed times.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Introduce the start/end ordering rule first as a warning or best-practice invariant.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The partial alternative is a warning-level invariant or implementation-guide rule. That would flag the same records without invalidating them, but it is incomplete because systems could still exchange base-valid R6 appointments with negative duration.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids hard validation failures but permits negative-duration appointments to remain valid base R6 data.

evidence.detail: R4 local constraints include app-2/app-3/app-4 but no start/end ordering invariant.
R6 adds error invariant `start.exists() implies start <= end`.
evidence.quote: The start must be less than or equal to the end

examples.examplesMd: The example is structurally valid in R4 with both start and end present, but violates R6 `app-5`.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds an error-level invariant requiring appointment start to be no later than end. This is a validation break for bad or ambiguous historical data rather than a serialization break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old data with reversed instants can be old-valid/new-invalid. R6-to-R4 representability is not a concern because R4 can carry the same values; R4 simply did not reject them at the base resource level.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Run a pre-migration data-quality check for appointments where `start > end`. Correct obvious transpositions, quarantine records whose intended duration cannot be determined, and add regression tests around equal start/end if zero-duration appointments are expected.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The rule could have been introduced as a warning to avoid hard validation failures. Making it an error is defensible because negative-duration appointments are usually invalid scheduling data.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds an error-level invariant that if `start` exists then `start <= end`. That can invalidate R4 instances with reversed start/end values, but those instances describe negative-duration appointments and are likely erroneous for normal scheduling. The invariant is a targeted data-quality rule on a narrow condition.
keyEvidence: R6 Appointment includes invariant `app-5` with expression `start.exists() implies start <= end`.
R4 Appointment does not have the same start/end ordering invariant.
The existing report classifies this as Medium impact and Justified.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 / trial-use means validators may encounter historical bad data, but the non-normative status and the clinical/operational value of preventing impossible time ranges support the stricter rule.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 data with `start` after `end` can become base-invalid under R6 validation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A warning-level invariant would be less disruptive, but it would continue to permit nonsensical negative-duration appointments as valid base data. The hard invariant is proportionate to the defect it prevents.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: I agree with the existing Medium impact and justified/Partial alternative judgment.

findings.title: `basedOn` now allows many request resources beyond ServiceRequest

justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of allowing appointments to be based on more request resource types is reasonable, and it does not invalidate R4 `basedOn` references because ServiceRequest remains allowed. The remaining concern is R6-to-R4 representability.

findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is safe for this element. R6-to-R4 strict validation fails for `basedOn` references to CarePlan, DeviceRequest, MedicationRequest, RequestOrchestration, NutritionOrder, or VisionPrescription unless they are moved or represented by extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For downgrades, preserve unsupported `basedOn` references in extensions or a related-resource mapping table. Do not coerce them to ServiceRequest unless a real equivalent ServiceRequest exists. Test each added request type.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This is an additive R6 capability. The only more downgrade-friendly design would be to keep R6 constrained to ServiceRequest, which would forgo the new modeling capability.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 widens `Appointment.basedOn` targets while retaining the R4 ServiceRequest target. That does not invalidate R4 Appointment instances. There is real R6-to-R4 downgrade loss if an R6 appointment is based on a CarePlan, DeviceRequest, MedicationRequest, RequestOrchestration, NutritionOrder, or VisionPrescription, but that is expected added expressiveness rather than a questionable R4-to-R6 base break.

R6 `Appointment.basedOn` retains ServiceRequest and adds CarePlan, DeviceRequest, MedicationRequest, RequestOrchestration, NutritionOrder, and VisionPrescription.

R6 adds occurrenceChanged.

examples.examplesMd: The example combines recurrence fields to show the downgrade gap. A real R6 instance may need to satisfy additional terminology expectations for recurrenceType/timezone depending on profiles and terminology services.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 introduces a native recurrence/series model for Appointment. It is additive for R4-to-R6 validation but materially changes what an Appointment can mean and what must be preserved during downgrade or cross-version synchronization.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No existing R4 instance fails solely because these optional fields exist. The break is representability: an R6 appointment series with recurrence templates, recurrence IDs, or series links cannot be encoded in base R4 Appointment without extensions or external state. R6 also adds a warning if an appointment has both an originatingAppointment and a recurrenceTemplate.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, define extensions for recurrenceTemplate, recurrenceId, occurrenceChanged, and appointment-series links, or maintain them in an external scheduling system. Test recurring-series creation, exception appointments, and downgrade/upgrade round-trips. Treat the `app-6` warning as a data-quality rule even though it is not an error.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because R4 had no equivalent core recurrence model, there is no fully backward-compatible way to add this expressiveness without extensions. R6's base additions are justified for scheduling but require explicit downgrade strategy.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The recurrence and series fields are optional R6 additions, so they do not invalidate R4 Appointment instances. They do, however, create a substantial R6-to-R4 conversion gap: native recurrence rules, occurrence changes, and appointment-series links cannot be faithfully represented in base R4 except by expansion, extension, or local policy. Because recurring appointments are a real scheduling need, the added R6 model is justified despite the downgrade burden.
keyEvidence: R6 adds recurrence/series elements including `recurrenceTemplate`, `recurrenceId`, `occurrenceChanged`, `originatingAppointment`, and `previousAppointment`.
R4 Appointment has no corresponding native recurrence-template element.
The existing report classifies this as High impact and says no R4-to-R6 compatibility alternative is needed.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3 / trial-use means Appointment scheduling behavior is mature enough that downgrade loss matters to mixed-version ecosystems. The finding is additive in the R4-to-R6 direction, so the FMM concern is about conversion and interoperability planning rather than invalidating old data.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 recurrence semantics cannot be losslessly represented in base R4 Appointment without expansion or extensions.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: There is no useful less-breaking base R6 design for R4 instances because the fields are optional additions. Using only extensions would preserve R4 shape but would fail to provide a standard computable recurrence model in R6.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the existing High downgrade impact and Not applicable alternative judgment, while emphasizing that this is reverse-conversion burden rather than an R4-to-R6 validation break.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and `abstract=false` are stable. R6 status changed from draft to active, which is a maturity/status change rather than an identity break.

No local Appointment minimum cardinality increased and no maximum cardinality decreased for common elements. `patientInstruction` widened from 0..1 to 0..* and is covered in its datatype finding. `participant` remains 1..* and `participant.actor` remains 0..1 with the same local app-1 type-or-actor invariant.

AppointmentStatus and ParticipationStatus code systems were compared and no code additions/removals were found despite version/status changes. `specialty` binding weakened from preferred to example and is recorded as non-breaking. Full expansions for broad value sets were not performed.

Local app-1, app-2, and app-3 are materially retained. New app-5 is reported as a finding. New app-6 is a warning tied to recurrence additions, and app-7 applies only to new `cancellationDate`. Base DomainResource constraints were excluded as inherited.
`supportingInformation` remains Reference(Resource) and `slot` remains Reference(Slot). Material target changes for `reason`, `basedOn`, and `participant.actor` are reported as findings.

No local Appointment element newly became a modifier or ceased being one. `Appointment.status` remains the local modifier element because of `entered-in-error`. Inherited modifierExtension/base changes are out of scope.

No material summary-flag change was found for common local Appointment elements that would by itself be a breaking change. New R6 elements have their own summary settings; inherited summary flag differences were excluded.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value constraints were found to have been added or removed on Appointment elements.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex changes were identified for Appointment elements.
No local Appointment slicing changes were found. Extension slicing inherited from base artifacts is out of scope.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Status value set versions changed but local code lists were unchanged
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The bindings remain required, but local CodeSystem comparison found the same AppointmentStatus and ParticipationStatus codes in R4 and R6. Version-pinned validators still need updated package versions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Refresh terminology package references from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4`; do not introduce code remapping for AppointmentStatus or ParticipationStatus based on the checked CodeSystems.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: `specialty` binding weakened from preferred to example
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Weakening a binding does not make old instances invalid; it loosens terminology expectations.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that treated the R4 preferred c80 practice code binding as a quality rule may need to decide whether to retain that rule locally despite the R6 base weakening.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.path: Appointment.class / account / subject / cancellationDate / virtualService / replaces
nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional operational fields
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: These elements are optional (`0..1` or `0..*`), so they do not make existing R4 instances invalid when moving to R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: They are R6-to-R4 downgrade risks. `class`, `account`, `subject`, `cancellationDate`, `virtualService`, and `replaces` need extensions or external state if R6 content must round-trip to R4.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Start/end comments now mention requestedPeriod fallback
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The datatype and cardinality of `start` and `end` are unchanged; the comment is guidance text. The actual hard validation change is the new `app-5` invariant, reported separately.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Review scheduling UI/business rules that infer requested periods when exact actual times are unknown.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The canonical identity, resource kind, type, and base definition are stable; status maturity alone does not change instance validity.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance processes may treat the R6 artifact as more mature, but migrations still need to account for the structural findings in this report.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Several high-impact local Appointment changes use `CodeableReference`. A datatype-level R4/R6 analysis should own any broader CodeableReference semantics, constraints, or serialization risks beyond the local element replacements reported here.

Inherited snapshot changes such as `language` binding, contained-resource text, modifierExtension summary/base decorations, and DomainResource constraints were intentionally excluded and should be handled by the base artifact reports.

R6 includes Appointment search-parameter changes related to service type references, reason, group, subject, and recurrence. Search parameters are outside this resource StructureDefinition report but may affect client/server migration.
R6 recurrenceTemplate introduces required/preferred terminology bindings. Full expansion and stability analysis would improve confidence for recurrence migrations and validators.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis used local computable artifacts and did not have an official R4→R6 Appointment diff, Jira rationale, or committee change notes. Justification assessments are therefore inferred from StructureDefinition content.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official FHIR change log/diff pages and Patient Administration work group rationale for Appointment changes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Only targeted CodeSystems for AppointmentStatus, ParticipationStatus, and ParticipantRequired were compared. Full terminology expansions were not run for example/preferred/required bindings such as encounter-reason, service-type, v3-ActPriority, recurrence type, timezones, week-of-month, and days-of-week.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology server expansions for both versions and compare code availability, designations, and binding semantics.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Narrative specification pages were not separately reviewed. Recurrence, virtual service, and subject/participant guidance may contain migration nuance not visible in the StructureDefinition snippets.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review build.fhir.org Appointment narrative pages and any cross-version mapping notes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build (`6.0.0-ballot4`) and may change before final publication.
